correctness.rationale: At q=0 the increments of 2Jk(N−k)−2hk have strictly positive sign through k=m=floor(N/2) and negative sign thereafter for both parities under 0<h<J. Every mixed configuration is strictly above all minus. Finiteness gives both separations uniformly for small q, with the two off-gate regions connected to their respective endpoints. For a decreasing distance kernel, each ordered pair distance within a subset is bounded below by its rank separation; equality for all pairs forces that subset to be an interval (including a singleton). Apply this to both parts of the cut to get precisely the two minimizing end intervals, both for r^(−q) at q>0 and for log(N/r). On the e^(−βH_q(E))/Z capacity scale, internal basin conductances grow at least as e^(βδ)/N, each gate edge has conductance at most 1/N, and a basin-constant trial potential has bounded scaled capacity. A minimizing potential therefore differs from its endpoint value by O(e^(−βδ/2)) along each fixed internal path. Clamping basin potentials changes the scaled gate energy by o(1), uniformly; the two minimizing stars give a positive lower bound, so the error is relative. A gate state has m and N−m edges to the two basins, giving effective weight π(S)m(N−m)/N² per serial proposal. The singleton capacity identity has numerator π(all minus)(1+o(1)); all plus has zero potential. The Taylor remainder βO(q²) vanishes for finite βq, and at βq→∞ every positive shape gap still has exponent tending to +∞. At fixed small q>0 only the two end intervals survive. The N=4 log-cut products are 12, 4 and 3, each twice, yielding the stated three levels.
residual_risks: Analytic review for fixed N and the stated serial time normalization only; finite checker inspected, not executed. No assertion at larger q, at the field boundaries, or in a simultaneous thermodynamic limit.
